name: WEDOS | Protection & Cache Performance
author: wedos.com

sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/wgpwpp directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Let the plugin guide you through the service setup process
sections.changelog:
v2.4.0

  • New: detection of the UpdraftCentral key compromise (October 2026): UpdraftCentral keys stored on the website, the hidden backdoor plugin and its secret accounts are shown on the dashboard and in an admin notice, with the steps to take. Read-only: the plugin never changes other plugins, keys or accounts

v2.3.2

  • Fixed: PHP notice “_load_textdomain_just_in_time was called incorrectly” (WordPress 6.7+ with debugging on), caused by translated cron interval labels while the plugin schedules its tasks during load

v2.3.1

  • Fixed: version 2.3.0 on WordPress.org was briefly published without the Recommendations files, which stopped websites that updated during that time
  • New: safety net: if any plugin file is missing (for example after an interrupted update), the plugin pauses itself and shows a notice instead of stopping the website

v2.3.0

  • New: Recommendations — WEDOS publishes signed recommendations, the plugin measures on your site whether they apply and you decide: Confirm or Ignore. Nothing changes without your confirmation and every change can be undone
  • New: first recommendation — requests for missing media files in wp-content/uploads (typically bots) get a fast 404 instead of starting the whole WordPress; applied at web server level (.htaccess) when the server supports it and a check proves it works, otherwise in PHP before the theme loads
  • New: server-level rules are removed again automatically when the plugin is deactivated or WEDOS withdraws the recommendation
  • Security: every request to the WEDOS backend now carries a per-install private key; the verification file publishes only its SHA-256 hash, so nobody else can request this site’s data by naming the domain. The key is created automatically on update and rotates with the verification token
  • Fixed: a failed verification token rotation no longer retries on every dashboard visit; the plugin re-syncs the backend once and retries after 24 hours

v2.2.3

  • Fixed: flushing the whole page cache from the admin bar no longer ends in a fatal error when another request removes a cache folder at the same time; the flush skips the missing folder and clears the rest
  • Fixed: cache maintenance and cache size calculation tolerate files and folders removed concurrently

v2.2.2

  • New: Protection Summary — the dashboard explains in plain words what the protection handled (passed, blocked, verified, logged) and why requests were stopped
  • New: visitor geography with per-country protection actions, connection overview (TLS, HTTP versions) and targeted-paths insight
  • New: security vulnerability scanning of installed plugins, themes and WordPress core against the WEDOS vulnerability feed, with protection-aware guidance
  • New: Site Snapshot daily health card (load time, TTFB, SSL, database, updates, admin accounts) with automatic anomaly notices
  • Improved: onboarding reliably detects an already protected website and opens the dashboard automatically
  • Improved: origin server IP detection never reports the protection edge address as the origin
  • Fixed: page cache no longer stores error responses (database errors, fatal errors); deployed cache runners update themselves
  • Fixed: the verification file is served by WordPress itself when file permissions prevent writing it
  • Security: hardened output escaping and input sanitization across the admin interface

v2.2.1

  • Improved: smart onboarding — the DNS setup step is skipped automatically when the domain already routes to WEDOS Protection (via A records or CNAME/ANAME), including domains protected under another account
  • Improved: DNS records are only required when the protection service reports a known actionable state; active domains are never asked for additional records
  • Improved: WordPress 7.0 compatibility and WordPress.org Plugin Check compliance
  • Fixed: minor onboarding and dashboard polish

v2.2.0

  • New: Visitor Geography section — interactive world map, top countries, top cities, top targeted URI paths with attack-pattern detection, threat distribution and connection quality breakdown (TLS version, encryption ratio, HTTP methods split)
  • New: Subscription plans — Free, Standard and Premium with 30-day free trial that can be started directly from the dashboard
  • New: Security email reports with selectable frequency (weekly or bi-weekly), delivered to the admin email on the configured day
  • New: Daily rotation of the .well-known verification token for hardened ownership proof
  • New: WGP CDN cache purge button — manually flush the Anycast CDN edge cache for sites with a provisioned WGP service
  • Improved: dashboard performance — backend responses are cached locally with smart invalidation on plan changes
  • Improved: refined entitlement system aligned with the subscription plans
  • Improved: clearer empty states and actionable first-check prompts across the dashboard
  • Fixed: numerous stability and UX improvements across onboarding, dashboard and trial activation

  • New: Weekly security reports — receive a weekly email summary of blocked attacks, traffic and protection status
  • New: Report a problem — submit feedback, bug reports or questions directly from the dashboard
  • Compatibility: minimum required WordPress version lowered from 6.9 to 6.7

sections.description:
Activate WEDOS Global protection — WAF, DDoS protection and CDN for your WordPress website.

WEDOS Global (CDN Cache & Security)

WEDOS Global Protection plugin helps site administrators activate WEDOS.protection from inside WordPress. The plugin provides a simple landing page for non-technical users, guided website and DNS setup, a dashboard with protection status, and a consent step before any external service activation request is sent.

Cloud WAF & DDoS Protection

By filtering traffic and blocking harmful cyberattacks on cloud servers, our WAF provides protection for your WordPress websites without putting any extra load on your local resources.

Global CDN Cache

The WEDOS Global CDN will ensure a significant increase of your WordPress loading speed, and better overall server response all around the world.

Links to Documentation and Other Sources

  • WEDOS Global
  • Knowledge Base
  • Community Help

External Services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

WEDOS Global Protection (plugin.wedos.global)

  • Verify domain ownership via a local verification file
  • Register and activate the domain protection service
  • Check the protection and DNS status

Data sent: domain name, server IP address, admin email address, unique request ID, and this installation’s private API key (proves the request comes from this site; only its SHA-256 hash is published in the verification file). No personal visitor data is ever transmitted.

WEDOS CDN (wp-cdn.wedos.com)

  • Serves WordPress core and WooCommerce static assets (JS, CSS) from WEDOS CDN edge nodes
  • Fetches a manifest file listing available asset versions and their SHA-256 hashes
  • Assets are only rewritten when local file hash matches the CDN manifest — no data about visitors is transmitted
  • CDN is opt-in and can be disabled at any time from the dashboard

Anonymous telemetry (plugin.wedos.global/cdn-plugin/telemetry.php)

  • Sends anonymous usage statistics once daily when opted in: plugin version, WordPress version, rewrite count
  • No domain name, no IP address, no personal data is included

Subscription management (plugin.wedos.global)

  • Used only when you start a free trial or subscribe to a paid plan (Standard, Premium)
  • Data sent: domain name, admin email address, selected plan identifier
  • Subscription status is queried periodically to determine which paid features (e.g. detailed visitor geography) are unlocked
  • The free plan does not require any subscription data exchange

Vulnerability intelligence feed (utils.wedos.tools/vulns)

  • Downloads a database of publicly known WordPress vulnerabilities (compiled from the Wordfence Intelligence feed, CC BY-ND 4.0) once daily
  • The comparison with your installed plugins, themes and WordPress core runs entirely locally on your server
  • Data sent: none beyond a standard HTTP request (no domain, no site data, no list of your plugins is ever transmitted)

Website performance check (utils.wedos.tools/api/v1/performance/)

  • Once daily measures your website’s public loading speed (TTFB, total time) from the WEDOS infrastructure for the Site Snapshot card
  • Data sent: your domain name only

Recommendations feed (plugin.wedos.global/recommendations/)

  • Downloads the list of WEDOS recommendations hourly; it is signed and verified before use, and contains only data, never code
  • Whether a recommendation applies is measured locally on your server; nothing is applied until you confirm it
  • Data sent when downloading: none beyond a standard HTTP request
  • When you confirm, ignore or undo a recommendation on a site registered with WEDOS Protection, the plugin reports the decision: domain name, recommendation ID, your decision, and the number and average duration of matching requests in the last 24 hours

Billing provider (FastSpring)

  • When you purchase a paid plan, your order is processed by FastSpring (fastspring.com)
  • FastSpring acts as the merchant of record for the transaction
  • See FastSpring’s privacy policy for details on data they collect during checkout

Bundled Third-Party Libraries

The plugin ships with the following open-source libraries (no external network calls — all bundled locally):

Chart.js 4.4.0 (MIT license)

  • Used for analytics charts (requests over time, top countries bars)
  • Source: https://www.chartjs.org/
  • License: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js/blob/master/LICENSE.md

jsvectormap 1.7.0 (MIT license)

  • Used to render the interactive world map in the Visitor Geography section (paid feature only — loaded when geographic analytics are unlocked by the active plan)
  • Source: https://github.com/themustafaomar/jsvectormap
  • Map data renders aggregated country traffic counts received from the WEDOS Global Protection backend; no visitor data is sent anywhere
  • License: https://github.com/themustafaomar/jsvectormap/blob/master/LICENSE

The service is provided by WEDOS Group SA, 7 Rue Robert Stumper, L-2557 Luxembourg, EU.

  • Terms of Service
  • Privacy Policy

By activating the plugin and clicking “Create request”, you explicitly consent to your domain data being sent to the WEDOS Global Protection service.

Bundled third-party libraries

All executable code ships inside the plugin package; nothing is loaded from external servers by default. For code review purposes, the bundled minified libraries and their unminified sources:

  • Chart.js 4.4.0 (MIT) — standard upstream UMD build, unmodified. File: assets/vendor/wedos-chart.umd.min.js (renamed copy of chart.umd.min.js). Source: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js/releases/tag/v4.4.0
  • jsVectorMap (MIT, license file bundled alongside) — standard upstream build plus the world map data file. Files: assets/vendor/jsvectormap/. Source: https://github.com/themustafaomar/jsvectormap
  • WEDOS vulnerability matcher (includes/Vuln/) — our own unminified GPL code, no third-party origin.

Optionally, the two UI libraries above can be served from the WEDOS CDN instead of the local copies. This is part of the documented WEDOS CDN service, is disabled by default, requires the user to enable it, and every CDN-served file carries a Subresource Integrity hash with an automatic fallback to the bundled local copy.

Free plan and trials: the plugin itself is fully functional free of charge. Paid features (such as the detailed visitor geography or targeted-path analytics) are capabilities of the hosted WEDOS Protection service, not of the plugin code. When a trial of the hosted service ends, the plugin keeps working on the free plan; no plugin functionality is time-locked.
